claim: Building 4-bit patterns from game bytes at run time costs too much per pass; make them once, keep them in spare pages and send with OTIR, and treat the cache miss cost rather than the hit rate as what sets pace.

evidence.text: Run-time building cost 113 T a byte at 28 MHz; made once and kept in spare pages, then OTIR, the pace came out within 0.07%.
evidence.quote: Made once and kept in spare pages, then OTIR: the hooks fit and the pace came out within 0.07%.

evidence.text: With 4-5 blocks the delay is only 33-66k T and with 6 or more there is none; per-update pattern uploads of about 20k T alone overran it, so an image-keyed pattern cache came before limiter tuning.
evidence.quote: per-update sprite pattern uploads (about 20k T) alone overran it, so an image-keyed pattern cache came before any limiter tuning.

evidence.text: Knight conversion cache misses were the cost: the +2.67 % was the image conversions.
